14"""HW MRADIX arg-sort for GCU400, written as TLE-Struct + TLE-Raw. 

15 

16``torch.argsort`` is ``torch.sort(...).indices``, so this is the same LSD radix 

17order as sort_mradix.py, but it is a separate Struct/Raw pair on purpose: with 

18no values to restore the pipeline loses its whole second output stream, and the 

19division of labour between the two sides changes with it. 

20 

21One hw thread per SIP owns a strided row set (persistent kernel, grid = 

22min(SIP_COUNT, M)); the TLE-Struct side converts one row to monotonic uint32 

23sort keys, stages keys + row positions into the four VDMEM ping-pong windows, 

24hands them to the TLE-Raw region (argsort_mradix_l1.tops) which runs ``ndigit`` 

25LSD radix passes on the hardware MRADIX unit, and then reads the sorted 

26positions back and stores them in the dtype torch asks for. 

27 

28What this buys over "sort(...)[1]", i.e. over running the sort kernel and 

29throwing its values away: 

30 

31 - no value output tensor and no value staging/writeback: the key readback, 

32 the dtype restore and the value store are all gone (that is roughly a 

33 third of the sort kernel's HBM traffic at 16 bits and half of it at 8); 

34 - the positions are stored straight from VDMEM, widened to int64 by this side 

35 when the row fills the tile (no per-lane predicate, so the backend's masked 

36 64-bit store, which drops lanes, is never used), left as int32 for a 

37 partial tile, and emitted by the region itself for a narrow-key row set, 

38 where a store issued from this loop is the slower path (see 

39 _IDX_IN_REGION_MIN_ELEMS); 

40 - 8-bit rows join the envelope. What kept int8/uint8 off the mradix path in 

41 sort is the byte-lane value writeback, which does not exist here, so an 

42 8-bit row is just a two-digit sort. 

43 

44Ordering contract: the MRADIX pass emits *descending* key order, so ascending 

45output sorts bitwise-inverted keys (``ASC``); the fold and the inversion are 

46bijections on the key width, so equal keys stay equal. LSD plus a per-lane 

47initial position keeps equal keys in row order, which is exactly 

48``torch.argsort(..., stable=True)``'s tie-break -- and a stable answer is a 

49valid answer for ``stable=False`` too. 

50 

51Capacity envelope (enforced by ``argsort_mradix_supported``, mirrored from the 

52raw region): ``N <= MAX_SORT_COLS`` (16384). Four ping-pong windows of BLOCK_N 

53uint32 elements are 16 bytes per element (the backend charges 29 bytes per 

54element, i.e. 29 * 16384 = 475136 of the SIP's 896KB VDMEM at the cap); 

55fp16/bf16 rows use the same window width because the region sorts on 32-bit 

56keys. Everything outside the envelope (int64, bool, rows longer than the cap, 

57non-last ``dim``) stays on the generic path in argsort.py. 

58""" 

59 

60import logging 

61from pathlib import Path 

62 

63import torch 

64import triton 

65import triton.language as tl 

66 

67logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

68 

69try: 

70 import triton.experimental.tle.language as tle # noqa: F401 

71 from triton.experimental.tle.language import raw as tle_raw 

72 from triton.experimental.tle.raw import dialect 

73 

74 HAS_TLE_RAW = True 

75except ImportError: # pragma: no cover - TLE is part of the gcu400 toolchain 

76 HAS_TLE_RAW = False 

77 

78_EXTERN_FUNC_NAME = "argsort_mradix_l1_kernel" 

79 

80VEC_LEN = 128 

81NUM_WARPS = 4 

82 

83# Same VDMEM budget as sort_mradix.py: four uint32 ping-pong windows, charged 

84# at 29 bytes of DSM per element, so BLOCK_N = 16384 is the largest power of 

85# two that fits the SIP's 896KB (29 * 16384 = 475136, 29 * 32768 overflows). 

86MAX_SORT_COLS = 16384 

87 

88# Whether the positions are emitted by the raw region instead of by the Struct 

89# loop, and whether the Struct side may widen them to int64 itself. 

90# 

91# Widening in the Struct loop is the cheaper of the two on its own (one 8-byte 

92# store from VDMEM instead of a 4-byte store here plus a separate read-4/write-8 

93# pass), and it is what all the 32-bit rows use. But a Triton-issued store 

94# inside this row loop collapses once the row set is large *and* the input is 

95# narrower than 32 bits: measured on the core harness, a 4096x4096 row set goes 

96# from ~1.3ms to ~4.7ms for fp16/int16 and to ~3.6ms for int8, while the same 

97# shape with an int32 input is unaffected. That is the same cliff sort hits 

98# (see _IDX_IN_REGION_MIN_ELEMS in sort_mradix.py), so at or above this many 

99# elements a narrow-key row set hands the positions to the raw region -- which 

100# writes them with 4-subthread vector stores -- and pays a separate cast. 

101# 

102# The threshold sits just above the largest measured "Struct store wins" point 

103# (1024x1024 = 1M elements), which keeps 4096x4096 (16M) on the region path. 

104_IDX_IN_REGION_MIN_ELEMS = 1 << 21 

105 

106# dtype -> width of the monotone sort key the launcher builds. A 16-bit key is 

107# zero-extended into a uint32 lane and needs four 5-bit digits; an 8-bit key 

108# needs two. Unlike the sort envelope this includes int8/uint8: no value is 

109# restored here, so the byte-lane store path that keeps them out of sort does 

110# not exist. 

111_KEY_BITS = { 

112 torch.float32: 32, 

113 torch.int32: 32, 

114 torch.float16: 16, 

115 torch.bfloat16: 16, 

116 torch.int16: 16, 

117 torch.int8: 8, 

118 torch.uint8: 8, 

119} 

120 

121if HAS_TLE_RAW: 

122 _TOPS_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("argsort_mradix_l1.tops") 

123 

124 # The raw region: argsort_mradix_l1.tops compiled as a standalone device 

125 # function. deferred=True makes the call site a dsl_region that is 

126 # materialized at the end of the pipeline instead of being inlined at the 

127 # call site, so the region can sit inside the row loop and is traced once, 

128 # not once per iteration. 

129 @dialect( 

130 name="tops", 

131 file=_TOPS_FILE, 

132 extern_func_name=_EXTERN_FUNC_NAME, 

133 deferred=True, 

134 ) 

135 def _edsl_argsort_mradix_l1(*args, **kwargs): ... 

136 

137 @triton.jit 

138 def _to_sort_key( 

139 x, 

140 KEY_BITS: tl.constexpr, 

141 MASK: tl.constexpr, 

142 TOP: tl.constexpr, 

143 SHIFT: tl.constexpr, 

144 ASC: tl.constexpr, 

145 ): 

146 """Monotone uint32 sort key, in the digit domain the raw region walks. 

147 

148 The transform is the classic sign fold: a floating-point value maps to 

149 its own pattern with the sign bit flipped for negatives; a signed 

150 integer maps to its pattern with the sign bit flipped; an unsigned 

151 value is already monotone. 

152 

153 Floating-point patterns are canonicalised first, because a rank order 

154 has to agree with the reference the accuracy tests compare against 

155 (CPU ``torch.argsort(stable=True)``), which is a *comparison* order: 

156 - every NaN maps to one quiet-NaN pattern. A plain sign fold is a 

157 bijection on the bit pattern, so it would order -NaN and +NaN 

158 separately, and -NaN would land at the *opposite* end of the row 

159 (its pattern folds to the smallest key). Since all NaNs fold to the 

160 quiet positive pattern they become equal, which puts them last 

161 ascending / first descending, and leaves their relative order to 

162 LSD stability -- exactly the reference behaviour. 

163 - -0.0 maps to +0.0. They compare equal, so they must carry the same 

164 key and let stability order them by position; folding the raw 

165 patterns instead would order them by sign bit. 

166 

167 ``ASC`` selects ascending output: the MRADIX pass emits descending key 

168 order, so ascending rows are sorted as bitwise-inverted keys. The fold 

169 and the inversion are bijections on the key width, so equal keys stay 

170 equal and LSD stability is preserved. 

171 

172 argsort needs no inverse: the key never leaves the VDMEM windows. 

173 """ 

174 # Widen to a 32-bit lane: the region counts 32-bit lanes, and a 16/8-bit 

175 # key only needs 4/2 of its digits (the zero-extended upper bits are 

176 # all zero and never contribute to a digit that matters). 

177 if KEY_BITS == 32: 

178 u = x.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True) 

179 elif KEY_BITS == 16: 

180 u = x.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.uint32) 

181 else: 

182 u = x.to(tl.uint8, bitcast=True).to(tl.uint32) 

183 # Canonicalise the floating-point patterns before the fold (see above). 

184 # The magnitudes are per-dtype: bfloat16 keeps the float32 exponent 

185 # width, which is why it cannot share the float16 constants. 

186 if x.dtype.is_floating(): 

187 if KEY_BITS == 32: 

188 MAG_MASK, INF_MAG, QUIET_NAN = 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x7F800000, 0x7FC00000 

189 elif x.dtype.is_bf16(): 

190 MAG_MASK, INF_MAG, QUIET_NAN = 0x7FFF, 0x7F80, 0x7FC0 

191 else: 

192 MAG_MASK, INF_MAG, QUIET_NAN = 0x7FFF, 0x7C00, 0x7E00 

193 mag = u & tl.full((1,), MAG_MASK, tl.uint32) 

194 u = tl.where(mag > INF_MAG, tl.full((1,), QUIET_NAN, tl.uint32), u) 

195 u = tl.where(mag == 0, tl.zeros((1,), tl.uint32), u) 

196 # hi is 0xffffffff (all ones) for a negative float / 0x80000000 (its 

197 # sign bit) for a non-negative one: `sign * MASK | TOP`. 

198 if x.dtype.is_floating(): 

199 sign = (u >> SHIFT).to(tl.uint32) 

200 hi = sign * tl.full((1,), MASK, tl.uint32) | tl.full((1,), TOP, tl.uint32) 

201 elif x.dtype.is_int_signed(): 

202 hi = tl.full((1,), TOP, tl.uint32) 

203 else: 

204 hi = tl.full((1,), 0, tl.uint32) 

205 k = u ^ hi 

206 if ASC: 

207 k = k ^ tl.full((1,), MASK, tl.uint32) 

208 return k 

209 

210 # The Struct side of the pipeline: one launch per shape, one raw call per 

211 # row. The loop lives here (not in the region) because this side owns the 

212 # VDMEM windows and the row mapping is then plain Triton arithmetic. 

213 @triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["M", "N"]) 

214 def argsort_mradix_l1_launch( 

215 input_ptr, 

216 output_idx_ptr, 

217 output_idx64_ptr, 

218 M, 

219 N, 

220 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

221 NVEC: tl.constexpr, 

222 KEY_BITS: tl.constexpr, 

223 MASK: tl.constexpr, 

224 TOP: tl.constexpr, 

225 SHIFT: tl.constexpr, 

226 ASC: tl.constexpr, 

227 NDIGIT: tl.constexpr, 

228 SRC_IS_B: tl.constexpr, 

229 IDX_IN_REGION: tl.constexpr, 

230 OUT_I64: tl.constexpr, 

231 ): 

232 row_base = tl.program_id(0) 

233 row_stride = tl.num_programs(0) 

234 # Exact trip count for this hw thread: no tail clamp, so every 

235 # iteration owns a real row. 

236 nrows = tl.cdiv(M - row_base, row_stride) 

237 # One allocation, four slices: tle.gpu.alloc rounds every buffer up, 

238 # while a single 4*BLOCK_N window pays that rounding once. The slice 

239 # offsets are multiples of BLOCK_N*4 bytes, i.e. 512B-aligned, which is 

240 # what the raw region's vector scatter needs. 

241 # 

242 # The windows are allocated by tl and handed to the region as pointers. 

243 # The region must not declare them __local__ as well: both allocators 

244 # start at VDMEM offset 0 and neither side knows about the other, so 

245 # raw static buffers would silently overlap these windows. 

246 buf = tle.gpu.alloc( 

247 [4 * BLOCK_N], 

248 dtype=tl.uint32, 

249 layout=None, 

250 scope=tle.gpu.smem, 

251 nv_mma_shared_layout=False, 

252 ) 

253 offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N) 

254 mask = offs < N 

255 k_pad = tl.zeros((1,), dtype=tl.uint32) 

256 i_pad = tl.full((1,), 0xFFFFFFFF, dtype=tl.uint32) 

257 offs_u = offs.to(tl.uint32) 

258 for r in range(0, nrows): 

259 row = row_base + r * row_stride 

260 # Key conversion (Struct): the row's own dtype -> monotone uint32 

261 # keys. Pad lanes take key 0, the last position of the descending 

262 # digit walk, and index 0xffffffff so a real key 0 outranks them. 

263 x = tl.load(input_ptr + row * N + offs, mask=mask, other=0) 

264 k = _to_sort_key(x, KEY_BITS, MASK, TOP, SHIFT, ASC) 

265 k = tl.where(mask, k, k_pad) 

266 iv = tl.where(mask, offs_u, i_pad) 

267 if SRC_IS_B: 

268 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (BLOCK_N + offs,)), k) 

269 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (3 * BLOCK_N + offs,)), iv) 

270 else: 

271 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (offs,)), k) 

272 tl.store(tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (2 * BLOCK_N + offs,)), iv) 

273 # The region runs NDIGIT passes and, by SRC_IS_B, always leaves the 

274 # sorted lanes in v_a/i_a. All four windows are declared as outputs, 

275 # which keeps its effects on them visible to the compiler. 

276 tle_raw.call( 

277 _edsl_argsort_mradix_l1, 

278 [ 

279 tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (0,)), 

280 tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (BLOCK_N,)), 

281 tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (2 * BLOCK_N,)), 

282 tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (3 * BLOCK_N,)), 

283 output_idx_ptr + row * N, 

284 NVEC, 

285 NDIGIT, 

286 # The region emits the positions only for a narrow-key row 

287 # set that is large enough to pay for the split; otherwise 

288 # it is handed 0 and the Struct side stores them below. 

289 N if IDX_IN_REGION else 0, 

290 ], 

291 output_indices=[0, 1, 2, 3], 

292 ) 

293 # Writeback (Struct): the sorted positions are the only output. 

294 # - the region already emitted them for a narrow-key row set 

295 # (_IDX_IN_REGION_MIN_ELEMS), so nothing happens here; 

296 # - a row that fills the tile is widened to int64 here; with no 

297 # per-lane predicate the 8-byte store is a plain vector store, 

298 # and this beats the region storing 32-bit positions plus a 

299 # separate elementwise pass that reads them back to write 8 

300 # bytes (an extra launch and an extra full read); 

301 # - anything else leaves int32: a *masked* 64-bit store loses half 

302 # of its lanes on GCU, so the widening is left to torch. 

303 if not IDX_IN_REGION: 

304 iout = tl.load(tle.gpu.local_ptr(buf, (2 * BLOCK_N + offs,)), mask=mask) 

305 if OUT_I64: 

306 tl.store(output_idx64_ptr + row * N + offs, iout.to(tl.int64)) 

307 else: 

308 tl.store( 

309 output_idx_ptr + row * N + offs, 

310 iout.to(tl.int32), 

311 mask=mask, 

312 ) 

313 # This barrier is load bearing, not just defensive: the raw region 

314 # deliberately leaves its last subthread barrier to this one, so 

315 # that the positions readback is ordered against the next row's 

316 # staging stores without paying a second per-row barrier inside the 

317 # region. 

318 tl.debug_barrier() 

319 

320 

321_MAX_GRID = None 

322 

323 

324def _max_grid(device_index=None): 

325 """Rows (hw threads) that can be in flight at once: one per SIP.""" 

326 global _MAX_GRID 

327 if _MAX_GRID is None: 

328 props = torch.gcu.get_device_properties(device_index) 

329 _MAX_GRID = int(props.sip_count) 

330 return _MAX_GRID 

331 

332 

333def argsort_mradix_dtype_ok(dtype): 

334 """Would the mradix kernel accept a row of this dtype?""" 

335 return HAS_TLE_RAW and dtype in _KEY_BITS 

336 

337 

338def argsort_mradix_supported(x): 

339 """Is ``x`` (last-dim, contiguous, 2-D) inside the argsort envelope?""" 

340 if not argsort_mradix_dtype_ok(x.dtype): 

341 return False 

342 if x.ndim != 2 or x.numel() == 0: 

343 return False 

344 n = x.shape[-1] 

345 if n <= 0 or n > MAX_SORT_COLS: 

346 return False 

347 if not x.is_contiguous(): 

348 return False 

349 return True 

350 

351 

352def argsort_mradix(x, descending, out_i64=True): 

353 """Rank the last dim of a contiguous 2-D view of ``x`` (stable, LSD radix). 

354 

355 Returns the positions as int64 when the row fills the tile (every power-of- 

356 two row, i.e. the common case) and as int32 otherwise; the caller widens 

357 the int32 case. 

358 """ 

359 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME ARGSORT_MRADIX") 

360 

361 n_rows, n_cols = x.shape 

362 block_n = max(VEC_LEN, triton.next_power_of_2(n_cols)) 

363 key_bits = _KEY_BITS[x.dtype] 

364 ndigit = (key_bits + 4) // 5 

365 grid = min(_max_grid(x.device.index), n_rows) 

366 # Narrow keys at a large row set take the same split sort uses: the region 

367 # emits 32-bit positions and torch widens them afterwards. Everything else 

368 # stores the positions from the Struct loop, widened when the row fills the 

369 # tile. 

370 idx_in_region = key_bits < 32 and x.numel() >= _IDX_IN_REGION_MIN_ELEMS 

371 out_i64 = out_i64 and block_n == n_cols and not idx_in_region 

372 out = torch.empty( 

373 x.shape, 

374 device=x.device, 

375 dtype=torch.int64 if out_i64 else torch.int32, 

376 ) 

377 argsort_mradix_l1_launch[(grid,)]( 

378 x, 

379 # OUT_I64 is a constexpr, so the dead half of the position writeback is 

380 # never traced and both pointers may carry the same buffer. 

381 out, 

382 out, 

383 n_rows, 

384 n_cols, 

385 BLOCK_N=block_n, 

386 NVEC=block_n // VEC_LEN, 

387 KEY_BITS=key_bits, 

388 MASK=(1 << key_bits) - 1, 

389 TOP=1 << (key_bits - 1), 

390 SHIFT=key_bits - 1, 

391 ASC=int(not descending), 

392 NDIGIT=ndigit, 

393 # An odd digit count starts in window B and an even one in window A, 

394 # so the last pass always lands in window A (see the raw region). 

395 SRC_IS_B=ndigit % 2, 

396 IDX_IN_REGION=idx_in_region, 

397 # OUT_I64 is the whole widening contract: it is only set when the row 

398 # fills the tile (no per-lane predicate, so the 8-byte store is a plain 

399 # vector store) and the region is not already emitting the positions. 

400 OUT_I64=out_i64, 

401 num_warps=NUM_WARPS, 

402 num_stages=1, 

403 ) 

404 return out
